abstract: Plasmids play a key role in prokaryotic evolution by providing adaptive traits that may facilitate colonization of new ecological niches. Members of the genus Pantoea harbor diverse plasmids, several of which carry metabolic and phytopathogenicity functions relevant for the interactions with plants and other eukaryotic hosts. Pantoea species harbor mobile plasmids that are able to transfer between cells, as well as domesticated plasmids that are vertically inherited, similarly to chromosomes. Although knowledge of Pantoea plasmid function and evolution is expanding, a general framework for their classification is still lacking. Here, we propose a framework for classifying Pantoea plasmids into plasmid taxonomic units (PTUs). By analyzing 797 publicly available Pantoea genomes, we identified 5,320 plasmids, of which 1,925 were classified by plasmid gene content similarity into 82 prevalent clusters of homologous plasmids. Integrating the clusters with plasmid backbone gene phylogeny, we recovered three previously described PTUs-LPP1, LPP2, and pOnion-across a broader taxonomic range than previously recognized. Additionally, three novel PTUs-LPP3, pPLD, and pINT-with distinct functional traits and pangenomic characteristics are proposed. We show that phylogenetic placement can assign previously unclassified plasmids to the plasmid groups defined here. Our analysis supplies a unified framework for plasmid classification in Pantoea and provides a foundation for future comparative studies of plasmid diversity and evolution in this taxon.
